checks: The projection gives exactly m integer columns at each of the two heights. Homothetic cubes give the real section radius by affine interpolation, and the sum of exact fiber volumes is 2(s^d+1). The specified y is outside every section since its first coordinate is at least 1.

The coordinate normals and their negative sum are rank d with unique positive relation. The caps vanish at the stated mark. The upper bound on every bottom margin and the lower bound on every top margin are strict for each θ in (0,1), including d=1, so the cap mass is exactly 2.

The equal-weight average gives height 1/2. True volume weights give height 1/(s^d+1) and the same horizontal mean. The interpolant agrees with the formula at each mean height and still excludes y. Direct rational evaluation confirms both weight identities and the mass ratio.

At the mean height the weighted sum of margins is u_i dotted with the weighted continuous average minus y. The average lies in Q, so indices 0 and 1 have probabilities one and zero. For i≥2 the independent symmetric coordinate sum has no atoms, giving probability one half.

Every original source union has probability one because top fibers are entirely inside every cap. Thus the respective defects are 0,1,1/2. Equal positive summation of the ambient margins and the exact equalizing x show whole-plane coverage exactly at h≥θ. Below the target fraction the bottom layer is still uncovered.

overlap.comparison: The older convolution construction takes a weighted centroid over an integer base. The current contact uses the weighted base mean only, with continuous coordinate y outside the interpolant, and demonstrates why aggregate light-fiber volume alone cannot force interior contact.

readability: The full rank and positive relation are for the continuous normals. The ambient weighted margin is nonzero off the contact height, permitting the bottom layer to be missed.

summary: The two-layer body realizes a full continuous-rank exterior contact with exact light cap masses, diffuse barycentric weights and the stated product probabilities.
